hints.title: Two-Pointer Interval Scanning
hints.text: Maintain pointers into both sorted disjoint interval lists and compute overlap between current intervals.

hints.title: Interval Intersection Bounds
hints.text: The intersection between intervals [s1, e1] and [s2, e2] is [max(s1, s2), min(e1, e2)]. It is valid if max(s1, s2) <= min(e1, e2).

hints.title: Earliest Endpoint Advancement
hints.text: Advance the pointer whose interval ends earlier: if e1 < e2, increment i; otherwise increment j. Continue until either list is exhausted.

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: M: length of first interval list
N: length of second interval list
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing all interval pairs takes O(M * N) time, ignoring the sorted disjoint nature of both lists.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Advancing the interval with the smaller end point guarantees linear O(M + N) traversal with O(M + N) output space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should articulate why advancing the earlier endpoint is correct: it cannot overlap with any subsequent interval.
complexity.notes: Closed intervals include endpoints: intersection can be a single point [x, x].
